Kuvitus: avaruudessa Aurinko vasemmalla: Illustration: in space, the Sun on the left and the Voyager 2 probe on the right, with a dashed line between them. Under the line are three rulers of the same length whose marks are spaced differently: the same distance in three different units.
Kaavakuva: suureen arvo on lukuarvo kert: Diagram: the value of a quantity is a numerical value times a unit. A pencil is measured with a ruler: the tip of the pencil is at the zero mark and the end edge at 12.0 cm, so the value of the length is $l = 12.0\,\text{cm}$. Below, the value is split into parts: $l$ is the quantity, $12.0$ the numerical value and $\text{cm}$ the unit. The ruler and the pencil are drawn to scale, horizontally 1 cm is 40 units.
Etuliitteet ovat kymmenpotenssien lyhent: Prefixes are abbreviations for powers of ten. The eight boxes show the factors nano $10^{-9}$, micro $10^{-6}$, milli $10^{-3}$, no prefix $10^{0}$, kilo $10^{3}$, mega $10^{6}$, giga $10^{9}$ and tera $10^{12}$. Between the arrows the factor grows a thousandfold at every step. In the bottom row the prefix is combined with the metre.
yksi askel oikealle = tuhat kertaa suure: one step to the right = a thousand times larger
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: sama etäisy: Diagram, not to scale: the same distance from the Sun to the Earth can be given in three ways. At the top a ray of light travels from the Sun to the Earth. Below, the distance $s$ is $1.496\cdot10^{8}\,\text{km}$, which is one astronomical unit $1\,\text{AU}$ and which light travels in 499 seconds, that is 8.32 minutes. The sizes of the Sun and the Earth and the distance between them are not to scale.
Kuva mittakaavassa: alumiinitanko viivai: Scale drawing: an aluminium rod next to a ruler. The ruler shows 0 cm to 15 cm, with numbers at every centimetre and small marks at every millimetre. The left end of the rod is at 2.0 cm and the right end at 13.6 cm, so the rod does not start at the zero mark.
